title: Concerns Raised Over O-Level English Oral Exam Discrepancies
description: The Singapore Ministry of Education (MOE) has addressed concerns regarding discrepancies in the O-Level English oral exam scores, stating that they are not technical in nature or due to malicious acts.

sections.heading: Background
paragraphs: The O-Level English oral exam has been a subject of discussion in Singapore, with 432 students reporting discrepancies in their scores.

sections.heading: MOE's Statement
paragraphs: According to CNA, the Ministry of Education (MOE) has clarified that the reported discrepancies are not due to technical issues or malicious acts.

sections.heading: Review of Processes
paragraphs: AsiaOne reports that the Singapore Examinations and Assessment Board (SEAB) is reviewing its processes following the reported discrepancies.

sections.heading: Parliamentary Discussion
paragraphs: The Straits Times mentions that Parliament is scheduled to discuss the concerns surrounding the O-level English oral exam.

faq.q: What is the issue with the O-Level English oral exam?
faq.a: There have been discrepancies reported in the scores of the O-Level English oral exam, affecting 432 students.

faq.q: What has MOE said about the discrepancies?
faq.a: MOE has stated that the discrepancies are not technical in nature or due to malicious acts, according to CNA.
SEAB is reviewing its processes in response to the reported discrepancies, as reported by AsiaOne.

faq.q: Is this issue being discussed in Parliament?
faq.a: Yes, the Straits Times reports that the Parliament will discuss the concerns regarding the O-level English oral exam.
